_what: The door on this computer through which a tool run reaches the person's own browser (browser-relay.mjs, ask-my-browser.mjs, computer-relay.mjs). While the browser extension holds its native messaging connection to the computer's host open, the host listens on loopback `host` at the port this computer's own report names under `port_name` (its `local_ports`; the number has that one home and is written nowhere here, and each tool row is given it by `{"fill": {"from": "computer", "field": "local_ports.<port_name>"}}`) and passes each `POST path` body { tool, input, request_key } to the extension over that connection, then answers with the extension's answer. `port_name` is also the name each tool row lists in `invoke.local_doors`. `tools` are the only tool ids the door passes on. A request body is at most `most_request_bytes`, an answer at most `most_answer_bytes` (the browser's own 1 MB limit on what a host sends it, and the larger of what a host may be sent), and a request waits at most `most_seconds` for the browser. Every word a caller reads is under `words`. A caller proves it is a run the engine started for this person (the engine's own way, `secrets:sign`, as tools/sign-a-mac-app-update does): it asks `challenge_path` for a nonce (good for `challenge_seconds`, once, at most `most_challenges` out at a time), signs `<nonce>\n<tool>\n<input as JSON>` with the Ed25519 key the person's vault holds under `key_name` (the row's right names that one key and that one operation; the private key never leaves the vault), and sends the signature as `signature` (hex) with the `nonce`. The door checks it against the key's public half, asked of the vault (`secrets:public` of `key_name`) at each opening of the door; the key is made once by the shared workflow make-a-signing-key-in-the-vault; a door whose vault holds no such key does not open. A request without a good proof is refused before the extension is told. `check_every_minutes` is how often the extension looks again for a connection it does not hold.

words.no_browser: No browser is connected to this computer. Open the browser the person is signed in to, with its extension allowed to talk to this computer, and ask again.
words.not_kept: This door does not pass on {tool}.
words.too_large_request: The request is larger than {bytes} bytes.
words.too_large_answer: The browser's answer is larger than {bytes} bytes.
words.too_slow: The browser did not answer within {seconds} seconds.
words.busy: The browser already has {count} requests waiting; ask again when one has finished.
words.not_json: Send one JSON object { tool, input } with content-type application/json.
words.not_here: This door answers only POST {path} from a program on this computer.
words.held: Another browser on this computer already holds the door to its browser; close it or this one will take it when it is free.
words.browser_left: The browser disconnected before it answered.
words.not_set_up: This computer's vault holds no key {key}, which lets tool runs reach its browser: run the workflow make-a-signing-key-in-the-vault with the name {key}.
words.no_proof: Send the nonce from {path} and a signature of it made with the key {key}.
words.bad_proof: The signature is not one the key {key} made for this nonce, tool and input, or the nonce was used or has expired.
words.no_port: This computer does not report a port named {name}; its owner adds {name} to the computer's report (local_ports).
